newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Sweden Feb trade surplus seen 10 bln Skr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sweden Feb trade surplus seen 10 bln Skr.

text.p: Sweden's trade surplus was expected to amount to 10 billion crowns in February, a Reuter poll of 14 analysts showed on Friday.
Forecasts ranged from nine billion crowns to 11.5 billion.
For the full year 1997, Sweden's trade surplus was expected to reach 124 billion crowns, according to a poll of seven analysts.
Forecasts ranged from 115 billion crowns to 130 billion.
In January, the trade surplus was 10.8 billion crowns and in February 1996 it was 9.4 billion crowns.
For the full year 1996, the surplus was 118.8 billion crowns.
Statistics Sweden will release the February trade balance data at 0900 GMT on March 25.

Economists and analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Chase, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, JP Morgan, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, Paribas, Salomon, S-E-Banken, and UBS Markets.
Full year forecasts were given by Carnegie, Den Danske Bank, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, and Salomon.
